_note: BLANK FORM for the configuration of an exercise. Copy it, rename it to scenario.json, replace the placeholders. Every list holds exactly one invented sample record — none of it comes from a real exercise. Rules: ../Schema/scenario.schema.json.

time_model._note: tick_minutes is the grid width. phases are the working windows; narrative_end is exclusive. business_day separately defines which time of day counts as working time for durations and daily rates.

phases.label: Day 1
phases.briefing: Text of the briefing mail for this phase.

control_ids._note: Identifier of the exercise control. It is not an actor and appears in no visualization. It receives both task reports and the infrastructure injects.

actors._note: order controls the reading order (aspects 1 and 2), color is optional — without it the dashboard assigns a palette color.
actors.name: Name of the role

actors._note: Second sample role so that the example message in communication.template.json has a recipient. Deliberately without color: without it the dashboard assigns a palette color by position.
actors.name: Name of a further role

components._note: depends_on names the components this one depends on. From that the dashboard computes the layers and arrows in aspect 4.
components.name: Name of the system

vocabulary._note: category determines the traffic-light color: ok, warning or critical. Every state used in the data must be listed here.

metrics._note: Binds a metric to events through selectors. pick: first, last or count — with count, end is omitted.
metrics.label: Label of the metric

cost_categories._note: For each category aspect 5 automatically creates a total tile, and a grand total on top of that when there is more than one.
cost_categories.label: Label of the category

costs._note: Rates instead of fixed amounts; the amount follows from rate × duration of the referenced metric. span.metric must not point at a count metric.
costs.label: Label of the cost item
